title: Types of vegetable production systems
competency: Describe the types of vegetable production systems in Ethiopia.

keywords.def: Collecting edible parts of wild plants, such as moringa leaves and sama.
Growing vegetables together with other field crops, such as Ethiopian mustard with maize.
Using land close to the homestead to grow vegetables for the household.
Market-oriented, intensively managed vegetable production, usually near towns.

en.text: Vegetable production evolved from gathering wild plants to specialized systems. In gathering, people collect moringa (shiferaw) leaves, sama (Urtica pilulifera), Amaranthus and wild fruits. Some vegetables grow mixed with field crops, such as Ethiopian mustard with maize, or taro and kale with coffee. Home gardens near the homestead, fed with household organic waste, are very common among Ethiopian smallholders. Commercial production is market-oriented, intensive in inputs and located near towns.

screens.title: Gathering and mixed cropping
paras: Production evolved from gathering wild plants to specialized systems.
1. Gathering wild vegetables: moringa (shiferaw) leaves, sama (Urtica pilulifera), Amaranthus.
Wild fruits are also gathered: shola, wild mango, dokma, agam, kega.
2. Mixed with field crops: Ethiopian mustard with maize; taro and kale with coffee.
Few vegetables grow in cereal fields; they are often on land unfit for cereals.
screens.note: The book lists shola, wild mango, dokma, agam and kega as wild vegetables; they are wild fruits.

screens.title: Home gardens and commercial farms
paras: 3. Home gardening is very common in Ethiopian smallholder farming.

notes.text: p.13: shola, wild mango, dokma, agam and kega are wild fruits, not vegetables in the book's own sense; moringa leaves, sama (nettle) and Amaranthus are the true wild vegetables. The book prints "Urticapilulifera" (should be Urtica pilulifera).
p.13: the heading says "mixed with cereal crops", but coffee is not a cereal (meaning: mixed with field crops). "are most of the times is grown" is ungrammatical.
